pl-l2d21c7-d1e108.summary: Holds that man, cast down by exterior temptation alone, deserved heavier punishment for falling by a lighter impulse; yet having some occasion of falling, he could be helped by grace to pardon, raised by another as he fell by another. The devil, sinning without a tempter, could neither be helped nor rise by himself, so his sin is irremediable.
claims: Man's fall by another's suggestion makes him redeemable.
The devil's unprompted sin is irremediable.

pl-l2d21c7-d1e111.summary: Adds that angelic nature, not wholly perished, was not redeemed; human nature, wholly perished, was redeemed in part, to make up the angelic ruin.
claims: Human nature is redeemed in part to replace fallen angels.

pl-l2d21c7-d1e116.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: since not all the angels perished, those who perished remain lost, and those who stood rejoice; but the rational creature in humans, wholly perished, was to be restored in part to supply what the angelic ruin diminished; so the saints are promised to be equal to the angels (Luke 20:36).
claims: Restored humans make up the angelic ruin.

pl-l2d21c7.summary: Holds that man, who fell by exterior temptation alone, deserved heavier punishment for falling under a lighter blow; yet, having some occasion of falling, he could be helped by grace to pardon, raised by another as he fell by another. The devil, who sinned without any tempter, neither deserved nor could have help, so his sin is irremediable. Also, angelic nature did not wholly perish, so it was not redeemed, while human nature wholly perished and so was redeemed in part, to make up the angels' ruin (Augustine, Enchiridion; equal to the angels, Luke 20:36).
claims: Man fell by exterior temptation only, which aggravates his fault.
Because he fell by another's suggestion, he could be raised by another.
The devil sinned without a tempter, so his sin is irremediable.
Angelic nature did not wholly perish and was not redeemed.
Human nature wholly perished and is redeemed in part to restore the angelic ruin.
